```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
```

## Question 1

##### Read and clean NY transit data

```{r NY_transit_data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
NYC_transit_df = read_csv(
  file = "data/NYC_Transit_Subway_Entrance_And_Exit_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(
    Route8 = col_character(),
    Route9 = col_character(),
    Route10 = col_character(),
    Route11 = col_character()
    )
  ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  
  select(
    line,
    station_name,
    station_latitude,
    station_longitude,
    route1:route11,
    entry,
    vending,
    entrance_type,
    ada
    ) |> 
  
  mutate(
    entry = case_match(
      entry,
      "YES" ~ TRUE,
      "NO" ~ FALSE
  )
)

NYC_transit_df
```

##### Description：

The cleaned NYC transit dataset contains `r nrow(NYC_transit_df)` rows, and `r ncol(NYC_transit_df)` columns. I cleaned variable names and retained the variables requested (line, station, name, station latitude, station longitude, routes served, entry, vending, entrance type, and ADA compliance). I convert variable `entry` from `YES` and `NO` character values to logical values (True and False). The data are not very tidy because the route information are stored in `route1` to `route11`. It will be better to store them separately as route name and route number.


##### How many distinct stations are there?

```{r }
distinct_station = 
  NYC_transit_df |> 
  distinct(line, station_name) |> 
  nrow()
```

There are `r distinct_station` distinct subway stations in the dataset.


##### How many stations are ADA compliant?

```{r}
ada_count = 
  NYC_transit_df |> 
  filter(ada == TRUE) |> 
  distinct(line, station_name) |> 
  nrow()
```

There are `r ada_count` ADA compliant stations.


##### What proportion of station entrances / exits without vending allow entrance?

```{r}
entry_proportion = 
  NYC_transit_df |> 
  filter(vending == "NO") |> 
  pull(entry) |> 
  mean()

entry_proportion = round(entry_proportion * 100, digits = 2)
```

The proportion of station entrances / exits without vending allow entrance is `r entry_proportion`%.


##### Reformat the route variables

```{r Tidy_NYC_transit}
NYC_transit_tidy = NYC_transit_df |> 
  pivot_longer(
    route1:route11,
    names_to = "route_number",
    values_to = "route_name"
  )
```

##### How many distinct stations serve the A train?

```{r}
A_station_count = 
  NYC_transit_tidy |> 
  filter(route_name == "A") |> 
  distinct(line, station_name) |> 
  nrow()
```

There are `r A_station_count` distinct stations serve the A train.

##### Of the stations that serve the A train, how many are ADA compliant?

```{r}
ada_A_train_count = 
  NYC_transit_tidy |> 
  filter(route_name == "A", ada == TRUE) |> 
  distinct(line, station_name) |> 
  nrow()
```

Of the stations that serve the A train, `r ada_A_train_count` are ADA compliant.



## Question 2

##### Read and clean the MR. Trash Wheel data

```{r mr_trash_data}
mr_trash_df = 
  read_excel(
    "data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel",
    range = "A2:N743"
    ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na(dumpster) |> 
  mutate(
    sports_balls = as.integer(round(sports_balls)),
    year = as.integer(year),
    trash_wheel = "Mr. Trash Wheel"
  )
```


##### Read and clean the Professor Trash Wheel data

```{r professor_trash_data}
professor_trash_df = 
  read_excel(
    "data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Professor Trash Wheel",
    range = "A2:M140",
    na = c("", "dive")
    ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na(dumpster) |> 
  mutate(
    trash_wheel = "Professor Trash Wheel"
  )
```


##### Read and clean the Gwynnda Wheel data

```{r gwynnda_data}
gwynnda_trash_df = 
  read_excel(
    "data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W",
    range = "A2:L395"
    ) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  drop_na(dumpster) |> 
  mutate(
    trash_wheel = "Gwynnda"
  )
```


##### Combine the three trash wheel datasets into a single dataset

```{r}
trash_wheel_df = 
  bind_rows(
    mr_trash_df,
    professor_trash_df,
    gwynnda_trash_df
  )
```


##### Calculate values for trash wheel dataset to answer questions

```{r}
professor_total_weight = 
  trash_wheel_df |> 
  filter(trash_wheel == "Professor Trash Wheel") |> 
  pull(weight_tons) |> 
  sum(na.rm = TRUE)

gwynnda_total_cigarette = 
  gwynnda_trash_df |> 
  filter(trash_wheel == "Gwynnda",
         year == 2022,
         month == "June") |> 
  pull(cigarette_butts) |> 
  sum(na.rm = TRUE)
```

The combined Trash Wheel dataset include `r nrow(trash_wheel_df)` observations and `r ncol(trash_wheel_df)` columns. Key variables include the Trash Wheel name, dumpster number, month, year, weight in tons, volume in cubic yards, and counts of different types of trash such as plastic bottles and cigarette butts. The total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel is `r professor_total_weight`. The total number of cigarette butts collected by Gwynnda in June of 2022 is `r as.integer(gwynnda_total_cigarette)`.




## Question 3

##### Read and clean the MCI baseline data 

```{r, message=FALSE}
mci_baseline_df = 
  read_csv(file = "data/MCI_baseline.csv",
           skip = 1,
           na = ".") |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  mutate(
    sex = case_match(
      sex,
      0 ~ "Female",
      1 ~ "Male"
    ),
    apoe4 = case_match(
      apoe4,
      0 ~ "non-carrier",
      1 ~ "carrier"
    )
  ) |> 
  filter(
    is.na(age_at_onset) | (age_at_onset > current_age)
  )
```

The cleaned MCI baseline dataset contains `r nrow(mci_baseline_df)` participants. It includes information on age, sex, education, APOE4 carrier status, and age at MCI onset. During data cleaning, I removed participants who
already had MCI at baseline and converted sex and APOE4 carrier status from numeric codes to categorical variables. 

##### How many participants were recruited, and of these how many develop MCI

```{r}
mci_count = 
  mci_baseline_df |> 
  filter(!is.na(age_at_onset)) |> 
  nrow()
```

Among the participants, `r mci_count` developed MCI during follow-up.

##### What is the average baseline age?

```{r}
avg_age = 
  mci_baseline_df |> 
  pull(current_age) |> 
  mean()
```

The average baseline age is `r round(avg_age, digits = 2)`. 

##### What proportion of women in the study are APOE4 carriers?

```{r}
women_count = 
  mci_baseline_df |> 
  filter(sex == "Female") |> 
  nrow()
  
women_apoe4_count = 
  mci_baseline_df |> 
  filter(sex == "Female",
         apoe4 =="carrier") |> 
  nrow()

women_proportion = women_apoe4_count / women_count
```

There are `r women_proportion * 100`% of women in the study are APOE4 carriers.


##### Read and clean the MCI amyloid data 

```{r, message=FALSE}
mci_amyloid_df = 
  read_csv(file = "data/MCI_amyloid.csv",
           skip = 1,
           na = c("NA", "Na")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  pivot_longer(
    baseline:time_8,
    names_to = "time",
    values_to = "amyloid_42_40"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    time = case_match(
      time,
      "baseline" ~ 0,
      "time_2" ~ 2,
      "time_4" ~ 4,
      "time_6" ~ 6,
      "time_8" ~ 8,
    )
  )
```

The cleaned amyloid dataset contains longitudinal measurements of the amyloid β42/40 ratio for each participant at 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 years after baseline. During import, I skipped the descriptive first row, treated `NA` and `Na` as missing values, cleaned the variable names, and change the repeated measurements into long format.


##### Check whether some participants appear in only the baseline or amyloid datasets

```{r}
baseline_only_count = 
  mci_baseline_df |> 
  anti_join(
    mci_amyloid_df,
    by = c("id" = "study_id")
  ) |> 
  nrow()

amyloid_only_count = 
  mci_amyloid_df |> 
  anti_join(
    mci_baseline_df,
    by = c("study_id" = "id")
  ) |> 
  distinct(study_id) |> 
  nrow()
```

There are `r baseline_only_count` participants who appear only in the baseline dataset and `r amyloid_only_count` participants who appear only in the amyloid dataset.


##### Combine the demographic and biomarker datasets

```{r}
mci_combine_df = 
  inner_join(
    mci_baseline_df,
    mci_amyloid_df,
    by = c("id" = "study_id")
  )
```

Count participants in the combined dataset

```{r}
combine_count = 
  mci_combine_df |> 
  distinct(id) |> 
  nrow()
```

The combined dataset contains `r combine_count` participants appear in both the baseline demographic and amyloid datasets. The data include baseline age, sex, education, APOE4 carrier status, age at MCI onset, follow-up
time, and the amyloid β42/40 ratio. Because the biomarker data are in longformat, each participant can appear once for each follow-up time point.


##### Export the combined dataset

```{r}
write_csv(mci_combine_df, "data/MCI_combine.csv")
```
